interface.title: Causal Method Advisor ("Which causal method fits my question?")
interface.field: Causal inference / econometrics / applied statistics (policy evaluation, A/B testing, observational studies)
interface.stage_of_work: Analysis planning: picking an identification strategy and estimator before estimating effects
interface.what_it_is_for: You give it a tabular dataset and a causal question in plain English (or Russian). It profiles the data, parses the question into treatment, outcome and other roles, runs assumption diagnostics, then recommends a causal method, gives a shortlist, or refuses, and explains why.

data.note: I used the built-in demo datasets. smoking.csv (California Prop 99, 1209 rows × 9 columns, panel of 39 states × 31 years) was analysed fully, twice. I loaded tax_instrument.csv (8000 rows × 8 columns), and its question filled in automatically, but its analysis was still on 'Profiling the data and running checks…' when I stopped. The demo picker is a scrolling list with about 8 entries visible at once, so the run did not count them; the repo's demos.json lists 12. I never uploaded the test file marketing_ab_test.csv.

features.name: Editable parsed-roles form with re-run
features.general: The system reads a free-text question and shows its interpretation as editable fields (cause, effect, extra variables, design flags). You fix any wrong field and run the analysis again with the corrected interpretation.
features.specific: In '1. How I understood the question', check Question type, Treatment (X), Outcome (Y), Instrument, Mediator and Threshold variable (column dropdowns), the 'Randomized?' radio (unknown/yes/no) and the 'A hidden confounder is suspected' checkbox, then press 'Re-run with these roles'. Only the checkbox was exercised in this run.
steps: Read the roles parsed from the question
Change a column dropdown or a design flag (e.g. tick the hidden-confounder box)
Compare the new verdict and scores with the previous ones
serves_tasks: Confirm how the question was understood
Declare a suspected unmeasured confounder and see how the advice changes

features.name: Verdict badge with ranked method-score bars
features.general: The recommendation appears with a confidence label (single recommendation, several options, or refusal), a written rationale, and a bar chart scoring each candidate that survived the rules.
features.specific: '2. Advice' shows a badge ('Recommendation' / 'Several good options'), text covering why it fits, the alternative, what to avoid and the assumptions to check, and beside it 'Method scores (rules have already removed impossible methods)' as progress bars (e.g. SDID 50%, SC 45%, DiD 5%).
steps: Read the rationale, alternative and 'Avoid' lines
serves_tasks: Read the verdict and the ranked candidate methods with their rationale
Declare a suspected unmeasured confounder and see how the advice changes

features.name: Assumption-diagnostics list with flag chips
features.general: A list of automatic checks run on the data, each with a plain-language result and short tag chips naming what was found, so you can see which assumptions hold before trusting the advice.
features.specific: '3. Assumption checks' lists sample size, pretrend test and sc pre fit, each with a sentence (e.g. 'gap drifts by -22.2 … p=1.15e-06') and chips such as policy_design, has_controls, single_treated_unit, pretrend_violated and sc_good_fit.
steps: Relate failed checks to the methods warned against in the advice
serves_tasks: Check the diagnostics behind the advice

features.name: Data-profile summary
features.general: An expandable plain-text summary of the dataset's structure and columns exactly as the recommender sees it, to confirm the data was read correctly.
features.specific: The 'Data profile (what the model sees)' expander shows rows, columns, structure (panel), unit and time (state(39), year(31), balanced), each column's type, range and missing %, and the treatment design group_post(california, after_treatment).
steps: Confirm the structure, unit and time variables
Check column types and missing percentages
serves_tasks: See the data summary the recommender worked from

features.name: Rule-filter audit table
features.general: A sortable, searchable table of every candidate method with a status icon (allowed / warning / forbidden) and the rule-based reason, so you can see why options were excluded.
features.specific: The 'All methods and the rules that filtered them' expander holds a table of method, status and why (✅ Synthetic control allowed; ⚠️ Difference-in-differences warning, 'pre-treatment trends are not parallel, so DiD will be biased'; ⛔ Causal forest forbidden, 'needs cross_section data, but the data is panel'). Its toolbar has show/hide columns, Download as CSV, Search and Fullscreen.
steps: Read the 'why' column for warned and forbidden methods
Use the toolbar Search to find a method
serves_tasks: See which methods were ruled out and why

features.name: Method reference cards
features.general: Expandable cards, one per suggested method, giving a short description, the estimand, the identifying assumptions, software libraries and further reading.
features.specific: Under '4. Methods' there is one expander per shortlisted method, e.g. 'Synthetic difference-in-differences — estimand: ATT', with its assumptions (parallel trends after reweighting, no anticipation, SUTVA), 'Python libraries: pysynthdid, cvxpy, statsmodels' and 'Read more: Facure ch. 25'.
steps: Open the next method's card to compare
serves_tasks: Read a reference card for a suggested method

features.name: Example-dataset picker with auto-filled question
features.general: Pick a bundled example from a labelled list; the matching question is filled in and old results are cleared.
features.specific: With the 'Demo dataset' radio selected, use the Demo dataset dropdown (e.g. 'tax_instrument.csv — Hidden confounder + instrument'); the 'Your question (English or Russian)' box fills in for that dataset.
serves_tasks: Choose an example dataset and its matching question

features.name: Data preview
features.general: An expandable preview of the loaded table, headed by its size, so you can inspect the columns before analysis.
features.specific: The 'Data preview: N rows × M columns' expander (e.g. 1209 rows × 9 columns for smoking.csv) shows the table with columns state, year, cigsale, lnincome, beer, age15to24, retprice, california, after_treatment.
steps: Check the size and column names
serves_tasks: Look at the raw table before analysing it

features.name: Recommender backend selector with help tooltip
features.general: A selector for which recommendation engine to use, with a tooltip explaining the available engines and what each needs to run.
features.specific: The sidebar Model dropdown offers only 'baseline (classical ML)'; its (?) tooltip says CausalGPT-mini needs PyTorch and models/causalgpt.pt.

Open the Model dropdown to see what is installed
